items.requirement: Switches each of the 20 ports from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V. The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V. Answered under Raised by P1: V282: From 0.8 V the switch turns on and carries the port's current. The 3.0 A and the 570 mV this question names apply from 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is a reported figure, not a requirement (owner, 2026-10-01)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: The continuous current one TPS55285 with its heatsink holds at 6.0 V in and 50 °C ambient, in A. This is each rail's continuous rating (owner, 2026-09-30). The heatsink's size is round 3's. Answered under Raised by P1: V281: 33 °C/W, the datasheet's RθJA on TI's 4-layer 2 oz EVM (SLVSI72A 5.3). The heatsink adds margin, which round 3 sizes (owner, 2026-10-01) V283: The rail's own latch: only that converter switches off, and it stays off until the operator clear control (F11) clears it. The other rails and the ESC keep running, and the firmware reports the trip (owner, 2026-10-01)

function the row names that P2 did not return: The Servo supply temperature line of IOBoard.md states that the trip latches until the operator clear control (F11) clears it, and 'threshold, latch and wiring of the alert outputs: a follow-up of R6'. V283 (owner, 2026-10-01) rules a latch of the rail's own: only that converter switches off and stays off until the F11 clear. found_values.value: Each servo rail delivers up to its own output current limit, set from 0.5 to 6.35 A in 50 mA steps (IOUT_LIMIT, reset 5 A, limit enabled), at the 5.5 V and the 8.4 V setting, from the DC input and from the pack (owner, 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-30). SLVSI72A states the limit's tolerance only at the 1, 3 and 5 A settings (4.7 to 5.3 A at 5 A, VIN 19 V, VOUT 5 V, engineering-sample characterization, note 1); none at 6.35 A. The continuous rating is V278's figure. Applied as 'Output current limit' of Servo supply
found_values.source: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md, Servo rail current (checkout 14098109c7ce); SLVSI72A rev A 5.4 (IOUT_LIMIT, note 1), 7.2, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf (vendors.py fetch, chrome, HTTP 200, 4,317,800 bytes)

found_values.value: From the pack at 8.4 V out with 6.0 to 8.4 V in the rail runs to its own limit (owner, 2026-09-30), and the average inductor clamp ILIM_AVG (7 A min, 8 A typ, no max) bounds what it delivers: at 6.0 V in, 4.57 A at 7 A and 5.15 A at 8 A, from the loss model of V111. 6.35 A at 8.4 V needs about 10 A of inductor current at 6.0 V and is not deliverable there. The continuous figure is V278. Applied as 'Output current from the pack at 8.4 V'

found_values.value: Derived from Figure 5-3 (VOUT 9 V, FPWM, TA 25 degC, typical), read from the PDF's vector curves: converter loss as a function of inductor current fitted to the VIN 5 V curve (boost mode, IL 0.94 to 7.73 A): P = 0.253 - 0.0973 IL + 0.0820 IL^2 W. The same fit predicts the VIN 9 V boost curves of Figures 5-5 and 5-7 within 0.13 W. At 6.0 V in and 8.4 V out: 93.2 % at 3.72 A out, 92.4 % at 4.11 A, 91.4 % at 4.57 A (IL 7 A), 90.2 % at 5.15 A (IL 8 A). At 8.4 V in (VIN 9 V curve): 95.2 % at 6 A. The data sheet guarantees no efficiency. Applied as 'Efficiency from the pack'

found_values.value: 5.5 V and 8.4 V are nominal set points; the highest voltage at a port's supply pin is the F16 ceiling, 6.0 V (LV) and 8.7 V (HV). SLVSI72A states no tolerance at 5.5 V or 8.4 V. Derived on the 10 V internal-feedback range from VOUT_FULL 9.85 to 10.15 V (VOUT_FS 01h, REF 0780h) and the VREF limits (1.117 to 1.141 V at 1.129 V; 0.837 to 0.855 V at 0.846 V; 0.501 to 0.514 V at 0.508 V): 5.5 V gives 5.40 to 5.59 V, 8.4 V gives 8.27 to 8.53 V. Ripple and load-step overshoot depend on round 2's output capacitors and are not included. Applied as 'Set point against the ceilings'
found_values.source: F16 Answer, Research.md (checkout 14098109c7ce); SLVSI72A 5.4 (VOUT_FULL, VREF), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf

found_values.value: An output of the main coprocessor's I/O expander with a pull-down that holds EN/UVLO below VEN_L 0.4 V while that output is an input (Measurement coprocessor reset row: the main coprocessor drives the converter enables through its expander, held off at reset). A MODE resistor of 0 Ohm (75h) or 48.7 kOhm (74h) sets the default OE bit to 0 (Table 6-2), so the output stays off after EN rises until firmware writes it. The rail's temperature latch (V283) also holds EN/UVLO low. Applied as 'Enable off at reset'
found_values.source: IOBoard.md, Measurement coprocessor reset, Load gates at reset (checkout 14098109c7ce); Pins.md, I/O expanders; SLVSI72A 5.4 (VEN_L, VEN_H), 6.3.2 Table 6-2, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf

found_values.value: 400 kHz (FSW 00b, 360 to 440 kHz). TI recommends a switching frequency below 500 kHz to reduce switching loss in high-power conditions (8.1) and uses 400 kHz in its application (8.2.2.1). The inner current loop needs L above 1.2/fSW: 3.33 uH at the 360 kHz minimum (8.2.2.3). Applied as 'Switching frequency' and the inductor's 'Inductance'
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.4 (fSW), 8.1, 8.2.2.1, 8.2.2.3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf

found_values.value: Above 13 A, the TPS55285's peak inductor current limit (typical; no min or max given): an overload or short drives the inductor to it. Highest peak in operation, derived with equations 5, 8 and 9 at 4.7 uH less 20 % (3.76 uH) and 360 kHz: 9.33 A for the adjustable supply boosting 6.0 V to 15 V at the 8 A typical clamp (ripple 2.66 A); 8.63 A for a servo rail 6.0 V to 8.4 V at the clamp; 8.15 A for 20 V to 8.4 V at 6.35 A. Applied as 'Saturation current'
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.4 (ILIM_PK, ILIM_AVG), 8.2.2.3 equations 5, 7, 8, 9, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf

GPA7 and GPB7 of the MCP23017 are output only (DS20001952D page 1) and the draft map puts no enable or input on them, so 14 lines a part and 3 parts. Applied as 'Lines'

found_values.value: 400 kHz. The only I2C rate in the tree is SET_I2C_KHZ, 100 to 400 kHz in 100 kHz steps, default 400, labelled for the display's bus; no other rate is stated. The TPS55285 takes 100 to 1000 kHz, the MCP23017 up to 1.7 MHz, the MCP9808 up to 400 kHz. Applied as 'I2C clock'

found_values.value: Yes. Each port switch limits its own current with its whole tolerance band between 3.0 A and 6.35 A: at or above 3.0 A the firmware abort acts first; under 6.35 A, the rail's limit, one shorted port does not pull the other ports into the converter's limit. The specification names the port switch's 3.96 to 4.84 A breaker (owner, 2026-09-30). Applied as 'Own current limit'
found_values.source: docs/Servo.md:35; IOBoard.md, Current aborts and Servo current ceiling (checkout 14098109c7ce)

The LV setting's low edge is 5.40 V (V114); the lowest operating voltage of the low-voltage servo read is 4.8 V (Savox SH-0255MG+: 'Operating Voltage (V) 4.8V - 6.0V'), 0.60 V less 30 mV in the 10 mOhm port shunt. Applied as 'Voltage drop'

The HV band is +/-0.99 % about 8.615 V, the LV band +/-3.5 % about 5.795 V. Ripple and overshoot narrow both and are not included. Applied as 'LV trip band' and 'HV trip band'

At the 3.72 A continuous rating it is 5.59 A at 6.0 V; in overload the average inductor clamp bounds it, 7 A min, 8 A typ, no maximum stated. 9.9 A is not reached while the clamp holds, but no maximum rules out a clamp above 9.9 A. Applied as 'Pack current at 6.0 V'

The capacitance a port presents is not found: no servo or receiver page read gives one. Applied as 'Inrush'
found_values.source: docs/Servo.md:66-69 (checkout 14098109c7ce); V109

found_values.value: 6.35 A as the TPS55285 output current limit setting, enabled at reset, with OCP_DELAY 128 us at reset (Table 7-4). It is a setting, not a bound: no tolerance is given at 6.35 A, and during the 128 us delay only ILIM_AVG (7 A min, 8 A typ, no max) bounds the output. The port switch's own limit (V123) acts first on one shorted port. Applied as 'Current into a shorted port'
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.4 (ILIM_AVG; IOUT_LIMIT note 1), 7.2, 7.4 (OCP_DELAY 00b = 128 us), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf; results/hardware/research/round1/FU-B1/030-adjudicator-R6.json

found_values.value: Cut-off state: yes, read from the port monitor's bus-voltage reading, which falls behind an open switch (an ESC's BEC on the pin, V126, holds it up instead). Jumper position: no; the setup screen lists the ceilings as set in hardware. Applied as 'Cut-off state readable'

found_values.value: 20 V. The TPS55285 programs up to 15 V, its output OVP trips at 110.5 to 120 % of the set point (18 V at 15 V), VOUT is rated 17 V absolute maximum, and a converter failed through passes the DC input, 20 V at most (V112). The same figure as R3's V44. Applied as 'Input withstand'
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 (VVOUT_OVP_FB), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf; V44 in results/hardware/research/round2/FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json

found_values.value: Requirement as the Follow-ups row and IOBoard.md state it: each of the 20 port switches switches its port from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V; with V282, from 0.8 V it turns on and carries the port's current, and V122's 3.0 A and V124's 570 mV apply from 5.0 V up. The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN from 2.7 V only (SLVSFC9C 6.3: 2.7 to 23 V), so it fails. Applied as 'Operating input range' and 'Conducts from 0.8 V'
found_values.source: Research.md, Round 2 Follow-ups row and V277, V282; IOBoard.md, Port supply switch (checkout 14098109c7ce); SLVSFC9C rev C (May 2026) 6.3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200)

found_values.value: 3.72 A: the continuous output current one TPS55285 holds at 6.0 V in, 8.4 V out and 50 degC ambient with the junction at the 125 degC recommended maximum on V281's 33 degC/W (IC loss budget (125 - 50)/33 = 2.27 W), with every converter loss in V111's model counted in the IC. 4.11 A if the DC loss of a 14.3 mOhm inductor (Table 8-2's XAL7070-472ME, maximum) is taken out of the measured loss; the Figure 5-3 conditions do not name the inductor. Both rest on typical curves at TA 25 degC: the rise of RDS(on) with temperature is not stated and not counted, nor is the heatsink, which round 3 sizes. Applied as 'Continuous current at 6.0 V in, 50 degC'
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.2 (TJ 125 degC), 5.3 (RthJA 33 degC/W on TPS55285EVM), Figure 5-3, Table 8-2, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf; V281 Answer (owner, 2026-10-01); scratch thermal3.py

found_values.value: 72.0 degC at the MCP9808 beside a servo converter, 66.25 degC beside the adjustable supply's converter: the highest settings, in the sensor's 0.25 degC steps, that hold the junction at or under 125 degC at the highest loss the converter reaches from 6.0 V, the 8 A typical inductor clamp (4.72 W at 8.4 V out, 5.23 W at 15 V out, V111 model). Derived TJ = Tboard + PsiJB x P with PsiJB 11.1 degC/W (EVM) and the sensor's +/-0.5 degC maximum error (-20 to 100 degC). The clamp has no maximum, so the bound holds only at the typical clamp. With 72.0 degC the trip limits sustained current at 50 degC ambient to about 2.47 A at 8.4 V from 6.0 V (Tboard = 50 + 21.9 x P degC). The alternative 99.25 degC (TJ 125 degC at the 3.72 A rating) holds V278's rating but lets TJ reach about 152 degC at the 8 A clamp before the trip. Which one applies is the owner's choice
found_values.source: SLVSI72A 5.2, 5.3 (RthJA 33, PsiJB 11.1 degC/W on TPS55285EVM), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf; MCP9808 DS20005095B Electrical Characteristics (TACY), Register 5-3, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/MCP9808-0.5C-Maximum-Accuracy-Digital-Temperature-Sensor-Data-Sheet-DS20005095B.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200, 14:00:08Z); scratch thresh.py

found_values.value: Requirement as stated: each port is cut off above 6.0 V (LV) or 8.7 V (HV), set by a jumper (F16), with V128's bands and V130's latch. A cut-off below the band would cut a rail set from 0.8 V (V55), so the ceiling acts above the band only. Applied as 'LV trip band', 'HV trip band', 'No cut-off below the band' and 'Latch until action'
found_values.source: Research.md, Round 2 Follow-ups row, F16, V280; IOBoard.md, Port voltage ceiling and Servo rail voltage (checkout 14098109c7ce)

found_values.value: Thresholds: INA3221 critical 3.0 A = 30.00 mV on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, compared on each conversion; warning 1.0 A = 10.00 mV, 250 counts, compared on the averaged value with AVG 4 (an exponential average, weight 1/4 a refresh, about 14.5 ms); INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV, 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV (ADCRANGE 1), on both paths (150 A x 200 uOhm, 300 A x 100 uOhm). Latching: the INA3221 critical and warning outputs transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state), because the main coprocessor times the critical line against the blanking time and the warning line against 400 ms, and a latched output would hold a line low after the current fell; the INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm only, because its line has no blanking, every stop latches (STATUS.md:340) and the latch holds the tripped part's node for the shift register; the firmware must then not poll DIAG_ALRT for CNVRF. Blanking time of the critical line: 5 ms. INA3221 in continuous shunt-only mode, CT 100 (1.1 ms typical, 1.21 ms maximum), 3 channels enabled on all 7 parts: one refresh is 3.3 ms typical, 3.63 ms maximum. A single conversion above 3.0 A holds a node low for one refresh, at most 3.63 ms, under the 5 ms and logged; two consecutive conversions hold it at least 6.6 ms (typical refresh), over the 5 ms, and abort. The minimum conversion time is not stated. Against the breaker: the critical threshold's error is 49.3 mA (INA3221 26.4 mA plus the port shunt's 22.9 mA), so it acts from 2.95 to 3.05 A; the TPS259474LRPWR breaker takes everything from 3.96 to 4.84 A in about 2 us with ITIMER open; the blanking applies to 3.0 to 3.96 A only, as the owner states
found_values.source: checkout 14098109c7ce: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:113, :387, :389; hardware/docs/Supply.md:27; STATUS.md:340; docs/Servo.md:35-36; INA3221 SBOS576C (Revised September 2026) 6.5, 7.3.2.1, 7.3.2.2, Table 8-34, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf; INA228 SLYS021A 7.6.1.12, 7.6.1.13, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf; TPS259474 figures as read by round 1 hardware/research/round1/FU-B1/023-P4-datasheet-R6.json

report.value: 5 ms. One INA3221 refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100) is 3.3 ms typical, 3.63 ms maximum: a single conversion above 3.0 A holds its node low for at most 3.63 ms and is logged; two consecutive conversions hold it 6.6 ms typical and abort. parts.refutation: Check 'Rail's own latch' fails: V283 requires only that converter to switch off and stay off until the operator clear control (F11) clears it. The MCP9808 has no such latch: comparator mode releases when TA falls below the limit less THYST; TCRIT forces comparator mode; interrupt mode (TUPPER/TLOWER) releases only on an I2C write of Int. Clear, which is firmware, not the F11 control; all registers return to defaults at power-on reset (VPOR 2.2 V, falling VDD). No sensor can meet it alone: the latch is a separate part, a function round 2 does not list. The other 9 checks pass.

data.ruling:
The refutation does not stand. The stock verifier confirmed the part and raised no refutation. The datasheet verifier failed one check, "Output current from the pack at 8.4 V". Its figure is right, but no requirement of this function asks for that figure.

(1) The figure is right. SLVSI72A 5.4 gives ILIM_AVG as 7 A minimum and 8 A typical, with no maximum, at VIN 8 V, VOUT 15 V and 400 kHz, in both FPWM and PFM. From the 6.0 V pack floor, a 7 A inductor current gives 5.0 A at 8.4 V without losses, and 4.44 A at 88.8 %. 8 A gives 5.71 A without losses and 5.07 A at 88.8 %. For 6.35 A at 8.4 V (53.3 W), the inductor needs 9.9 A at 90 %, above the 8 A typical. The verifier's 4.58 A and 5.16 A use its typical loss fit and fall inside these bounds. So no TPS55285 is shown to reach 6.35 A at 8.4 V from 6.0 V.

(2) No requirement of this function asks for it. Five passages in the checkout say so:
- The "Round 2" section of Research.md overrides the category rows. Its Follow-ups row for Servo supply (Research.md:583) and V278 (Research.md:984; for research on V281's 33 degC/W) set the requirement. That requirement is the continuous current one TPS55285 with its heatsink holds at 6.0 V in and 50 degC ambient, in A, as each rail's continuous rating. The verifier re-derived it as 3.72 to 3.74 A (4.11 to 4.13 A once the inductor's DC loss is taken out) and marked it as a pass.
- IOBoard.md:379, "Servo converter input from the pack", records the same clamp arithmetic as a known property of the part. It says 7 A gives 5.0 A, or 4.44 A at 88.8 %, and that 6.35 A needs 10.0 A, above the 8 A typical. Its open item is the continuous current the follow-up finds, with the temperature shutdown above it. Reaching 6.35 A from 6.0 V is not the open item.
- IOBoard.md:359, "Pack path current", says: "The converters' inductor clamps, 8 A typical each with no maximum, hold the draw lower where they act". The owner's design expects the clamp to act from the pack.
- IOBoard.md:71 and :377, and the owner's Servo rail decision in STATUS.md:45, state "from the pack each runs to its own limit too, because the SLS XTRON pack's 90 A carries all four converters". The same rows give the 4.44 to 5.0 A clamp figures at the floor. "Its own limit" therefore means the configured limit is not lowered when the rails run from the pack. It does not promise 6.35 A at 6.0 V in.
- The owner kept this fixed input after round 1 refuted it, with these figures already on the page. Research.md:565 says that if R6 leaves the part refuted, the owner decides with the continuous current the runs return.

The verifier read the "own limit" sentence as a requirement of 6.35 A at the pack floor. That reading overrides the follow-up requirement and the clamp figures that the specification itself records, so this check fails no requirement.

What the owner should see, recorded but not a failure: the peak a rail reaches at 8.4 V from the 6.0 V floor is set by the inductor clamp. That is 4.44 to 5.0 A at the 7 A minimum. 6.35 A is reached only from about 8.1 V in, the verifier's figure, which I did not re-derive. The continuous rating at 6.0 V in and 50 degC is 3.72 A. That is a thermal limit, and it is lower than the clamp limit.

The other 19 datasheet checks agree and pass, among them the allowlist (Texas Instruments, S1). On the stock side, the JLCPCB stock reading of 2732 passes the gate of 100 for 20 placements, and presale is 2724. The held 12 do not cover the 20 placements on their own. TI's status is ACTIVE and Digi-Key's is Active. No end-of-life notice is on the product page or at Digi-Key. TI's PCN listing was not read: both TI PCN URLs the verifier tried returned HTTP 404. The LCSC number C52160906 matches.

Scope is function, because the only question was this function's current requirement. Nothing about the part itself fails.

data.ruling:
The refutation does not stand. Its one failed check is "Rail's own latch". It applies the latch of V283 to the sensor. The specification puts the latch in a separate element that the alert sets. IOBoard.md, Servo supply temperature, says "Each alert output switches its own converter's output off above a threshold, in hardware" and asks "whether the alert sets the interlock's latch or a latch of the rail's own". V283 answers "The rail's own latch". So the alert sets the latch; the sensor is not the latch. The sensor itself is the owner's choice: the MCP9808T-E/MS beside each TPS55285, 4 a board (owner, 2026-09-30; Follow-ups row). The verifier states that no sensor can meet the check alone.

The datasheet facts the verifier read hold:
- Comparator mode releases below the limit less THYST (0, 1.5, 3 or 6 degC).
- Above TCRIT the output is forced to comparator mode.
- In interrupt mode, the alert stays asserted after TA < TCRIT - THYST until the controller writes Int. Clear (CONFIG bit 5) over I2C.
- A falling VDD below VPOR = 2.2 V resets CONFIG to 0x0000: alert disabled, limits unlocked.

So the part alone does not hold the rail off until the F11 operator clear. That is a fact about the function's wiring, not a failure of the sensor. What the sensor must do is set the rail's latch, and the verifier's other checks pass on that:
- an open-drain alert, polarity selectable
- TCRIT forced to comparator mode
- thresholds in 0.25 degC steps
- +/-0.5 degC maximum from -20 to 100 degC
- Crit. Lock and Win. Lock

The stock verifier confirmed every gate: JLCPCB 764 >= 100, Digi-Key 21,419, In Production, Active.

The rail's own latch remains a gap. No round 2 function lists it, and no part is selected for it. It is not known until a follow-up adds the latch part, for example a flip-flop the alert sets and the F11 clear resets. The pages should state that as not known, not drop the sensor.

Scope is function: the ruling is about this function's requirement, not about the part's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity.

data.ruling: The refutation holds. Its main point is an omission. Research.md row V111 (R6, Servo supply) asks which efficiency the converter's pack figures use from 6.0 to 8.4 V in at 8.4 V out, and its answer is "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". A value marked for research is a requirement input that P2 finds and applies, and the P4 datasheet verifier must re-read it. The claimed list has 19 entries. None has V111 as its source, and none is named for efficiency. The list does use values that depend on efficiency: "Pack current at 6.0 V" (V132), and the continuous current at 6.0 V in, which takes the loss on V281's 33 degC/W (V278). Round 1's list for the same function had "Efficiency from the pack", sourced V111, in FU-B1/002-P2-R6.json. The second point is weaker but also holds, because the list is incomplete. It gives "Output current limit" only as "up to 6.35 A". The specification sets 4 to 6.35 A for each rail (IOBoard.md line 377) and 0.5 to 6.35 A in 50 mA steps for the adjustable supply (line 380; line 71). The list carries the adjustable supply's 10 mV voltage steps but not its current-limit floor or step. Both defects are in the function's requirement list, not in the TPS55285 itself, so the scope is the function.
data.evidence: Research.md line 817, V111: "What efficiency do the servo converter's pack figures use from 6.0 to 8.4 V in at 8.4 V out, in %: 90 %, or the figure R6 reads from the TPS55285 datasheet (for research)?" Its answer is "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". No entry in the claim cites V111 or names efficiency. The claim does cite the neighbouring rows V109, V110, V112 to V117, V120, V131, V132, V134, V278, V281 and V283. Research.md line 66, P4 row: the datasheet verifier "re-reads each value found for research". Round 1's FU-B1/002-P2-R6.json lists the requirement {"name": "Efficiency from the pack", "value": "the data sheet's figure for 6.0 to 8.4 V in, 8.4 V out", "source": "V111"}. Its found value for V111 is "88.8 % ... Applied as 'Efficiency from the pack'". IOBoard.md line 379 still treats the efficiency as an open input: "at the 88.8 % R6 reads as typical at 25 degC, 4.44 A. The datasheet guarantees no efficiency". IOBoard.md line 377: "4 to 6.35 A a rail ... its limit stops at 6.35 A". IOBoard.md line 380: "a current limit of 0.5 to 6.35 A in 50 mA steps, both set from the display over I2C (SLVSI72A 7.2)". IOBoard.md line 71: "0.8 to 15 V and 0.5 to 6.35 A ... runs 4 to 6.35 A". SLVSI72A section 7.2, IOUT_LIMIT register, matches line 380: "sets the target output current limit from 500mA to 6.35A. One LSB stands for 50mA". The claim's "Output current limit" entry reads only "up to 6.35 A at every setting, from either source".

data.ruling:
The refutation stands. Both verifiers' refutations hold.

1) Stock, sourcing rule 4. JLCPCB's exact match for C2887910 (INA228AIDGSR, Texas Instruments, VSSOP-10) has stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -236. Under rule 4 a negative presale count fails whatever the stock says. The gate is 50 for this function: 5 boards (S7) x 1 placement = 5, and S4 never goes under 50. The gate is also 50 for the part at 2 a board (IOBoard.md:112). Stock 0 is under the gate either way. The rule-5 second vendor has no stock either: Digi-Key reads 0 in tape and reel, cut tape and Digi-Reel, with a 20-week lead time. The part is not held. The Held parts table and inventory-2026-09-25.csv have no INA row, so rule 6 does not apply. IOBoard.md:458 records that the owner expects the part back in stock soon. That is a statement, not a dated held quantity, so it does not pass rule 6.

2) Datasheet, against the series resistance the owner decided for this function. IOBoard.md:464 (owner, 2026-09-30) puts 1 kOhm in series with IN+ and with IN-, and a TVS behind them. SLYS021A section 8.1.4 and Figure 8-1 say "Do not use values greater than 100 ohms for RFILTER. Doing so will degrade gain error and increase non-linearity." 1 kOhm is 10 times that limit. RDIFF is given only as a typical 92 kOhm, with no minimum, maximum or drift. 2 x 1 kOhm therefore reads 92/94 = 0.979 of the true value, 2.1 % low (typical), and its drift over temperature has no bound. IOBoard.md:464 itself says the INA228's guidance was not read.

3) Datasheet, input withstand. The value found for V179 (FU-B3/005-P2-R8.json) is 85 V between the leads in either polarity, and 85 V from either lead to ground. SLYS021A 6.1 rates the differential input at -40 to 40 V and allows 5 mA into any pin. 85 V is 45 V over the differential rating. Through 1 kOhm alone, 85 V drives 85 mA (lead to ground) or 42.5 mA (across the inputs), 17 and 8.5 times 5 mA. The part only survives the fault with the TVS behind the resistors, and no run selects that TVS. IOBoard.md:464 leaves its connection, part and clamp voltage to round 2. I did not need, and do not rule on, the verifier's extra claim of -67 V on VBUS from a reversed lead.

Checks that pass: lifecycle (Digi-Key Active, not end-of-life, not discontinued), Texas Instruments on the S1 allowlist, and the LCSC identity (C2887910 is INA228AIDGSR). No part-level cause fails.

Scope is function. Rule 4 is a gate on the function's need (boards x placements), and the page counts quantity as function scope. The datasheet failures are against this function's own 1 kOhm series resistors and V179. This follows the round 1 ruling on the same function for the INA238 (FU-B3/024-adjudicator-R8-2.json). The owner fixes the INA228 (Scope, 2026-09-30). The clash between the owner's 1 kOhm and the datasheet's 100 Ohm limit, and the zero stock, go to the owner.

The datasheet verifier's only failed check is a disagreement on the noise figure. The verifier itself recorded passes true. The figure P2 states, 80 uV p-p (8 mA), is 4 times the plotted 20 uV p-p (2 mA) at the 1.1 ms conversion time. That error is in the conservative direction. Both values are below the 20 mA p-p research figure for the port current reading: V174 is "for research", and the host model assumes 0.02 A p-p (IOBoard.md, Not known). SBOS576C states no noise maximum, so no guaranteed figure is in conflict. The disagreement corrects the recorded figure to about 20 uV p-p (about 2 mA on 10 mOhm, typical, from the plot) and does not refute the part. The other 15 datasheet checks and all 13 stock and lifecycle checks agree and pass, as the verifiers report. This ruling re-read only the noise evidence. INA3221AIRGVR stays for "Port current monitor".
data.evidence: SBOS576C ("MAY 2012 - REVISED SEPTEMBER 2026"), page 18, Figure 7-7 "Noise Versus Conversion Time", rendered at 400 dpi, no averaging, 1000 conversions. The 1.1 ms trace (the CT=100 setting the design uses) has a flat baseline at about -95 uV, with single-conversion spikes to about -85 uV (5 of them) and about -105 uV (4 of them). That is about 20 uV p-p, about 2 mA on the 10 mOhm port shunt. The 332 us trace lies between about -40 and 0 uV, about 40 uV p-p. The 140 us trace lies between about 30 and 110 uV, about 80 uV p-p. The stated 80 uV p-p therefore matches the 140 us trace and not the 1.1 ms trace. The text around the figure (7.4.2 area) gives no numerical noise specification, and section 6.5 gives no noise maximum. Requirement: V174 (Research.md:880), "What accuracy and noise, in mA, must a port current reading hold?", is answered "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". IOBoard.md, Not known: "The host model assumes 0.02 A peak-to-peak sensor noise". 2 mA (plot) and 8 mA (stated) are both under 20 mA p-p.

data.ruling: The refutation holds. V177 asks whether each motor shunt sits in the pack's positive lead or in its return, and its answer is "for research" (owner, 2026-09-28). The claim says "high side on both paths", but none of its cited sources states where either shunt sits. The claim is an inference, and the inference does not follow from the sources. testbench/WIRING.md:37-47 says only that the ESC pack's return reaches the star point on its own lead. A low-side shunt in that lead, between pack negative and the star point, fits that wiring equally well. F7, the R3 row and IOBoard.md make the pack switch high-side. That fixes the switch position and says nothing about the shunt position. F15 gives only the 67.2 V pack voltage. IOBoard.md:508 states outright that the shunt position is not stated in the tree, and Research.md V189 repeats this. No other page in the checkout fixes the position either: Power.md names the shunt parts but not where they sit. The value "high side on both paths" is therefore not found, and V177 stays open. As the verifier notes, the 67.2 V common-mode figure still stands as the worst-case design basis. The INA228 is decided, and its bus input is rated to 85 V (IOBoard.md:452). The ruling is limited to this function's answer, so its scope is function.
data.evidence: Research.md:883 V177: "Does each motor shunt sit in the ESC pack's positive lead (high side) or in its return (low side)? ... for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". IOBoard.md:508: "Whether the shunts sit on the high side or the low side of the motor supply: not stated in the tree (R8)." WIRING.md:37-39: the "servo supply's return and the ESC pack's return ... all return to [the star point], each with its own lead". This gives no shunt position. Research.md:677 F7 and IOBoard.md ESC pack gate rows: "A high-side switch". This concerns the switch, not the shunt. Research.md:685 F15: 16 cells, 67.2 V. Research.md:895 V189 question: "Which side of the motor supply the shunts sit on is not stated". Its answer puts the cell monitor on the pack's negative behind an 85 V isolation barrier. That is consistent with either shunt position. A grep for shunt in hardware/docs and docs found no line that fixes the motor shunts' side.
